accuracy.evidence: The three rounds and their order are checked against Pearson and Gallagher (1983), who named the gradual release of responsibility, and Fisher and Frey's 'I do it, we do it, you do it' framing. Rosenshine (2012) Principles of Instruction is the source for modelling, guided practice and independent practice once success is high. Scaffolding (adult support that is withdrawn as the child takes over) is Wood, Bruner and Ross (1976). The EEF (2018) metacognition guidance names modelling as recommendation 3. The adult text does not claim fixed numbers of repetitions.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented failure points of guided instruction named in the adult text: one demonstration followed by solo work (the order scene refuses You do in first or second place with 'trying alone before you have seen it and shared it means guessing'), a passive we do round (the 'Grown-up, you draw it' button on the child's turn is refused), help sought before any attempt (Hint is refused until a real go, after Newman's work on adaptive help seeking), and never asking when truly stuck (challenge 'Keep quiet and guess' is refused).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagido lives the three rounds on one concrete skill: a modelled cat drawing with spoken steps and a recall check, a turn-taking drawing where the child's turns are enforced, a solo drawing with a dashed-outline hint gated on a prior attempt, a three-way round sort of everyday scenes and a round-ordering scene. It is not the practice-over-time lab (388 flagprac) or think, pair, share (1053 flagtps); the 6-token shingle gate reports no lab above 30% overlap.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child experiences each round before it is named in the DONE line: they only watch in scene 1, they must place the ears and whiskers themselves on their turns in scene 2 while the grown-up draws the head and eyes, and in scene 3 they place all four shapes alone. Wrong shapes are refused with the reason (everything sits on the head, so it comes first), and the hint appears as a dashed outline only after a try.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'The grown-up does them all' for we do (refused when the child asks the grown-up to draw on their turn), 'Ask for help straight away' (Hint before a go is refused with 'Your try shows you what you remember'), and 'Yes, one watch is enough' to skip to you do (placing You do first in the order scene is refused).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions checked in the browser, each wrong option tagged with its own slip and message: skip (skips the shared round), stuck (watching more does not teach your hands), passive (in we do you do your share), tryfirst (have a go first), giveup (stuck is normal, giving up stops the learning), round (says why the scene is I do), nowatch (I do comes before we do) and neverask (after a real go, ask).

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and everyday words for 6 to 8 year olds, within the family kid limit; lab text is one to two short sentences per scene and cards are under twelve words. Adult text stays within the adult limit while naming the precise terms: gradual release of responsibility, modelling, guided practice, independent practice, scaffolding.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph does one job (the three rounds, then one paragraph per round). Adult paragraphs give the research basis, what the adult does in each round, the named mistakes with what a good hint looks like, and what the lab does. The content gate finds no filler phrase.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px and 390 px phone screenshots in light and dark for all five scenes: the grown-up figure and step bubble sit left of the drawing paper, the three to four shape chips fit in one row below with readable names, the three round boxes fit side by side under the scene card, and the three order slots stack full width with their one-line job text.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Next step, one button per answer naming the step, 'Grown-up, you draw it' and one button per shape, a Hint button, one button per round naming the card, and one per round card to place next. The canvas aria-label carries each scene description and every piece of feedback, the challenge feedback is a role=status live region, right and wrong carry ✓ and ✗ as well as colour, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes.

Rosenshine, B. (2012) Principles of Instruction: research-based strategies that all teachers should know. American Educator 36(1)
Fisher, D. and Frey, N. (2013) Better Learning Through Structured Teaching: a framework for the gradual release of responsibility (2nd ed.)
Wood, D., Bruner, J. S. and Ross, G. (1976) The role of tutoring in problem solving. Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry 17, 89-100
Education Endowment Foundation (2018) Metacognition and Self-Regulated Learning guidance report, recommendation 3 (modelling)
